guide.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Xero, so you always need your own Xero app. Creating the app and connecting it to Composio is easy and free (about an hour). The hard part is production scale: past the 5-connection Starter plan you need a paid plan, and higher plans need App Certification and a security assessment. No source gives a certification timeline.

composio.note: Bring-your-own OAuth2 only. Create the app as a Xero 'Web app', then paste the client ID and secret into a Composio auth config with 'Use your own developer authentication' checked. The Xero toolkit lists 0 triggers, so trigger polling speed does not matter here.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed Xero app, so every Composio connection to Xero needs your own Xero app with its own client ID and secret.
reasons: No Composio-managed OAuth exists for Xero.
Xero does not support API keys, so OAuth 2.0 with a registered app is the only route.
Connection caps, rate limits and fees are measured per app, so your own app's plan decides how many customers you can connect.

scenarios.label: Prototype on demo company (Starter)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Building or testing an agent against Xero's demo company or your own trial org, with 5 or fewer connections.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured; c3, c4, c12

waiting.basis: The Starter plan lists no prerequisites or payment method (c7, c8).

scenarios.label: Small production, up to 50 connections (Core)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Real customers connect, you need more than 5 connections, and you stay at or under 50.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count: Starter steps plus adding a card (c9). Not measured.

waiting.basis: Whether Core needs certification is unclear. The pricing table lists none for Core, but the research notes say it does (see open questions).

scenarios.approval: A payment method is required. App Certification for Core is unconfirmed.

scenarios.label: Scaled or listed app (Plus and above)
scenarios.when_this_applies: You need more than 50 connections, or premium features such as Journals, the XPM API or bulk connections.

hands_on.basis: Estimate only: certification and security assessment work. Xero publishes no effort figure (c10, c11).

waiting.basis: No source in the dossier gives a certification or assessment timeline.

scenarios.approval: App Certification (Plus, Advanced, Enterprise), plus an initial and annual Security Assessment (Advanced, Enterprise). Premium features also need use-case approval.

prerequisites.title: Xero account and demo company
prerequisites.detail: Sign up for a free Xero account. Xero recommends the demo company for development; the alternative is a trial or paid org.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and API key
prerequisites.detail: You need these to create the auth config, and to copy the callback URI from your dashboard.

prerequisites.title: Credit card (Core and above)
prerequisites.detail: Card details are required when moving from Starter to Core.

prerequisites.title: Your own domain (optional)
prerequisites.detail: Only needed if you want to proxy the OAuth callback so the browser stays on your domain.

steps.title: Create the Xero app
steps.detail: Log in to the Xero Developer Portal, click New app, and choose integration type 'Web app'. Enter an app name and your company or app URL. Create the app, then generate a client secret.
steps.done_when: You hold a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Copy the Composio callback URI and add it to the Xero app
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from your Composio dashboard rather than typing it. The Composio guide shows https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. It must be https with no trailing slash. An agent can check the string you pasted against what Composio shows.
steps.done_when: The redirect URI is saved in the Xero app and matches Composio exactly.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Draft the minimal scope list for your use case, for example accounting.transactions, accounting.contacts and offline_access. offline_access is needed to refresh tokens. Premium endpoints such as Journals need extra approval.
inputs: List of Xero actions the agent must perform
steps.done_when: You have a reviewed scope list.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create an OAuth2 auth config for the xero toolkit with your own client ID, secret and scopes. This can be done through Composio's API or dashboard. Do not use Bearer Token. Store the resulting ac_ ID in your secret manager.
steps.done_when: You have an auth config ID starting with ac_.

steps.title: Optional: proxy the callback through your domain
steps.detail: Set the Xero redirect URI to your own endpoint and have it 302-redirect the query string to Composio's callback. An agent can write the endpoint. Whether Xero requires this is not confirmed.
steps.done_when: A test connection completes with the callback on your domain.

steps.title: Connect the demo company and test
steps.detail: Run a Connect Link flow and authorize the demo company. Stay within the 5-connection Starter cap, the per-tenant rate limits, and the 5000/day per-tenant limit.
steps.done_when: A tool call returns demo data.

steps.title: Add a payment method and move to Core or higher
steps.detail: Needed once you exceed 5 connections. Core is listed at $35 AUD per month, tax exclusive.
steps.done_when: The plan shows as active in the developer dashboard.

steps.title: Prepare certification materials
steps.detail: Read the certification checkpoints page and draft a checklist, plus a security-controls summary for the assessment. Avoid any design that trains models on Xero data.
steps.done_when: You have a checklist and draft documents ready to submit.

steps.title: Submit certification and security assessment
steps.detail: Submit through Xero's process. Click submit and handle any legal or business details yourself.

steps.title: Wait for Xero review
steps.detail: Review time is not documented in the sources read.

traps.title: Rate limits can't be raised
traps.detail: Limits are 60 calls/min and 5000/day per tenant and are the same for every app. Batch writes, paginate and use If-Modified-Since.

traps.title: Starter caps connections at 5
traps.detail: Beyond 5 connected orgs you must move to a paid plan. One Stack Overflow report suggests demo companies may count toward connection caps, but that is not confirmed for the current model.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: Composio's guide says https and no trailing slash. A mismatch will break the callback.

traps.title: No AI/ML training on Xero data
traps.detail: The updated terms prohibit using API data to train AI/ML models. Check your agent design against this.

traps.title: Composio default scopes and quota don't apply
traps.detail: With no managed app, you choose the scopes and get your own app's quota, so there is no shared Composio quota to worry about.

traps.title: Composio holds tokens server-side
traps.detail: Composio stores and uses the OAuth tokens on its servers. Xero's policy on server-side access is not confirmed in the sources read.

blockers.what_it_means: You hit the Starter connection cap.
blockers.what_to_do: Add a payment method and move to Core (50 connections), or a higher plan.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the current connection count against the plan caps.

blockers.what_it_means: You exceeded a per-tenant or app-wide rate limit.
blockers.what_to_do: Honour the Retry-After header, batch writes, paginate and use If-Modified-Since.
blockers.agent_can_help: Add retry and backoff logic and request batching.

blockers.symptom: Journals, XPM or bulk connections unavailable
blockers.what_it_means: These premium features need a security assessment and use-case approval.
blockers.what_to_do: Plan for the Advanced plan and its assessment before relying on these endpoints.

blockers.what_it_means: The URI in the Xero app does not match the one used by Composio.
blockers.what_to_do: Recopy the URI from the Composio dashboard and remove any trailing slash.

open_questions: Certification and security assessment timelines are not documented in the sources read. Check the certification checkpoints page or ask Xero developer support.
The researcher notes say Core requires App Certification, but the pricing table lists it only for Plus and above. Confirm with Xero.
Xero's redirect URI and domain rules were not verified. Test a callback on your own domain, or read the Xero OAuth docs, which did not render during research.
Xero's customer-side restrictions (admin consent, multi-org) were not verified. Review the Xero OAuth 2.0 docs.
The pricing table gives a Starter rate limit of 1000/day per org, while the limits FAQ says 5000/day. Confirm in the developer dashboard.
Xero's stance on server-side token storage by Composio is unconfirmed. Ask Xero support if your certification depends on it.
